## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Esoteric sūtra translated by **Amoghavajra** ([不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA)) in which **Avalokiteśvara** speaks the **Samantabhadra** (普賢) dhāraṇī. The interesting feature of this text is the **transposition** of the speaker: in most Samantabhadra dhāraṇī literature it is Samantabhadra himself who speaks the dhāraṇī (as in the *Avataṃsaka* "Practice of Samantabhadra" chapter); here Avalokiteśvara is the speaker, signalling a reframing of the Samantabhadra dhāraṇī within Avalokiteśvara-centric Esoteric practice. Compare [KR6j0236](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0236) *Qīngjìng Guānshìyīn pǔxián tuóluóní jīng* (T1038) by Zhìtōng, which has a parallel concept under a different title.

**Abstract**

The text fits within Amoghavajra's broader Avalokiteśvara liturgical corpus (cf. [KR6j0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0228)–[KR6j0231](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0231)) but differs in that the dhāraṇī-content is the *Samantabhadra* dhāraṇī rather than an Avalokiteśvara-specific dhāraṇī. The integration of Samantabhadra-dhāraṇī content into Avalokiteśvara-speaker frame reflects the increasing fluidity of the Esoteric maṇḍala-system in the eighth century, where major bodhisattvas could function as speakers of one another's dhāraṇī within ritually-flexible *yoga-tantra* configurations. The presence of a parallel text [KR6j0236](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0236) under Zhìtōng's earlier authorship suggests that this conceptual transposition was already being made in the seventh century; Amoghavajra's translation simply gives it a fresh recension within the Tángmì framework.
